description: Rule registry for the own parts. An error rule carries non-inferred evidence, a check and both fixtures, and its check is seen failing on its fail fixture (scripts/verify.mjs). A warn rule carries evidence. Evidence ids are entries of evidence/ledger.json; check and implementedBy paths are relative to skills/apple; fixtures name cases in fixtures/<part>/cases.json.

rules.statement: Under reduced motion, or when a muted inline play() probe is rejected (blocked autoplay, iOS Low Power Mode), the scene stays in normal flow at its end state and requests no scrub film.
rules.values: end state = progress 1; no film request

rules.statement: The scene does not pin when the viewport is shorter than the stage's content height plus the sticky offset (the page's sticky chrome).
rules.values: pin only when stage height + sticky offset <= viewport height

rules.statement: The scene box is its travel plus 100vh, its sticky child fills the viewport below the sticky offset (100vh, lvh or svh) and stays put for the whole travel, and progress stays in [0, 1] and never runs backwards on a forward sweep.
rules.values: box = travel + 100vh; sticky child = 100vh minus the offset; progress in [0, 1], monotonic

rules.statement: Every scrub file has a closed GOP with a keyframe at least every 8 frames, yuv420p pixels, no audio stream and, in MP4 or MOV, the moov box before mdat.
rules.values: keyframe at least every 8 frames; closed GOP; yuv420p; no audio; moov before mdat

rules.statement: Every set of sources for one film includes an H.264 file; HEVC, VP9 or AV1 never ship alone.
rules.values: an H.264 source in every set

rules.statement: The scrub driver never writes currentTime while the element is seeking (a latest-wins queue applies the newest target on seeked) and never calls fastSeek().
rules.values: 0 currentTime writes while seeking; 0 fastSeek() calls

rules.statement: The film is seekable wherever it is served: loaded into a Blob URL or MediaSource, or fetched with 206 byte-range responses.
rules.values: a Blob URL, MediaSource or 206 Range responses

rules.statement: The start image is frame 0 of the film or image sequence (SSIM at least 0.99 as displayed), and the video or canvas stays hidden until it has presented or drawn its first frame.
rules.values: SSIM at least 0.99; shown after the first presented or drawn frame

rules.statement: Prefer a closed GOP of 6 frames, 5 above 30 fps; all-intra costs about 2.9 times the bytes for little gain on hardware decode.
rules.values: GOP 6, or 5 above 30 fps; all-intra about 2.9 times the bytes

rules.statement: Keep a scene's travel within 70-300vh; a longer scene asks the reader to scroll through too little change.
rules.values: travel 70-300vh

rules.statement: Map scroll to progress directly, or smooth it with a time constant (about 100 ms), never with a per-frame factor whose speed depends on the refresh rate.
rules.values: no smoothing, or time-based with a time constant of about 100 ms

rules.statement: Use image sequences only for short films, alpha or software-decode targets, and show the decoded-memory budget (frames x width x height x 4 bytes).
rules.values: 1.95-5.3 times the bytes of GOP-6 video, by content; frames x width x height x 4 bytes decoded; a window of (2 x radius + 1) decoded frames

rules.statement: Test stacked backdrop blur over a moving stage on a software-rendering proxy; it can collapse to a few frames per second there.
rules.values: frame rate measured on a software proxy

rules.statement: Do not make VP9 the default scrub codec: it seeked slowest of the measured codecs; list H.264 first.
rules.values: H.264 first in source order

rules.statement: Put CSS scroll-driven animation inside @supports (animation-timeline: view()) over a finished static layout, and check that fallback in Firefox.
rules.values: inside @supports over the static layout

rules.statement: Tag scrub files with bt709 primaries and matrix and a transfer characteristic, so the film and its sRGB start image show the same colours.
rules.values: bt709 primaries and matrix; sRGB transfer tag

rules.statement: An HEVC scrub file uses the hvc1 sample entry and a closed GOP.
rules.values: hvc1; closed GOP

rules.statement: Every demo clip ships an H.264 High file in yuv420p with limited range (never yuvj420p or 4:4:4) and the moov box before mdat, and every other file of the set is 4:2:0 in limited range.
rules.values: H.264 High; yuv420p, limited range; moov first

rules.statement: A muted or decorative clip carries no audio stream.
rules.values: no audio stream; measured waste 32.5-43.7 % of the file

rules.statement: Every file carries the three colour tags, written with setparams and read back: bt709 primaries and matrix, and a bt709 or iec61966-2-1 transfer.
rules.values: bt709 primaries and matrix; transfer bt709 or iec61966-2-1

rules.statement: The start image of a clip is its frame 0, with an SSIM of at least 0.99 against that frame as a browser shows it.
rules.values: SSIM at least 0.99 against frame 0

rules.statement: A demo clip below the fold has no autoplay attribute, preload="none", no poster attribute (its start image is a lazy or , since a poster is fetched at load) and no source until it comes near, so 0 video bytes load before the reader scrolls; it gets its source once near. Scrub films and videos inside a scroll scene follow launch-scroll's rules instead.
rules.values: no autoplay attribute; preload none; no poster attribute; no source until near; 0 video bytes before scroll

rules.statement: A clip that moves on its own for more than 5 s (any loop, or a longer one-shot) has a way to pause it: native video controls, which pause from the keyboard, or a visible, labelled control that can be reached with Tab and pauses the playing clip on Enter or Space; and under reduced motion no clip plays by itself, also after it has loaded.
rules.values: native controls or a labelled, keyboard-operable pause control above 5 s; nothing autoplays under reduced motion, also after load

rules.statement: A rendered master has duration x fps frames at twice the slot's CSS pixels, with every image painted in every frame, and never comes from the built-in page recording (VP8 at 25 fps in CSS pixels). A video master is flagged as that recording by a heuristic, VP8 at 25 fps, which another VP8 file at 25 fps also matches.
rules.values: duration x fps frames; 2x the slot; every image painted; not VP8 at 25 fps

rules.statement: Direct a demo as short beats with readable holds: transitions of 300-500 ms, holds of at least 1 s (1.5 s for a result), typing at 8-12 characters per second, one cursor move of 0.3-0.8 s per target, no cut or zoom, loops of 4-8 s.
rules.values: transitions 300-500 ms; holds at least 1 s, 1.5 s for a result; typing 8-12 characters per second; cursor moves 0.3-0.8 s; loops 4-8 s

rules.statement: Keep each file inside its slot's budget: a tile 120 KB, a 5 s tile 250 KB at 1x or 600 KB at 2x, a card 400 KB, a device screen 700 KB, a hero under 2 s 300 KB at 1x or 1 MB at 2x.
rules.values: tile 120 KB; 5 s tile 250 KB at 1x, 600 KB at 2x; card 400 KB; device screen 700 KB; hero under 2 s 300 KB at 1x, 1 MB at 2x

rules.statement: Deliver 1.3-2.0 video pixels per CSS pixel of the slot.
rules.values: 1.3-2.0 video px per CSS px

rules.statement: Render and encode UI demos at 30 fps; 60 fps costs about 34 % more bytes and suits only fast motion graphics.
rules.values: 30 fps; 60 fps about 34 % more bytes

rules.statement: When an AV1 file ships, list it first (it is about 55 % of the H.264 bytes at equal quality) and always end the sources with H.264, since WebKit plays AV1 only with a hardware decoder.
rules.values: AV1 about 55 % of the H.264 bytes; H.264 last

rules.statement: A loop's seam, its last frame against frame 0, scores an SSIM at least the clip's median for consecutive frames (about 0.995); measured seams of 0.714-0.971 were visible.
rules.values: seam SSIM at least the consecutive-frame median (about 0.995)

rules.statement: A transparent clip ships HEVC with alpha before VP9 with alpha, then H.264 flattened over the page colour: VP9 alpha turns opaque in WebKit, and HEVC alpha encodes only through VideoToolbox, outside the agent sandbox.
rules.values: HEVC with alpha first; VP9 with alpha second; H.264 flattened last

rules.statement: A demo clip scrolled into view plays once at least half of it is visible.
rules.values: plays at half visible or more

rules.statement: The page requests, declares and lists no SF Pro, SF Pro Icons or SF Symbols font, in any spelling or URL encoding of the family name, loads no font from an Apple host and shows no Apple private-use glyph; every font stack starts with system-ui or a licensed font.
rules.values: no SF font request, @font-face, stack entry or glyph; stack starts with system-ui or a licensed font

rules.statement: Without script and under reduced motion, every heading, lede and call to action that the full page shows is visible at load, in normal flow, with no opacity, filter, clip or transform hiding it; entrance states hide content only behind a capability set by script.
rules.values: visible at load without script and under reduced motion; opacity 1

rules.statement: Every font size on the page comes from the page's chosen token set, every token size sits on the type ladder (the shipped one or the project's own), and every line height is a whole number of pixels.
rules.values: font sizes within 0.5 px of a token size; line height an integer number of pixels

rules.statement: Text reaches at least 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text, in the light and the dark scheme, against the backgrounds and opacities stacked under it, and against the worst background pixel inside its box when it sits over an image, gradient, pseudo-element, filter or fixed box; text over video or animated backgrounds, or in a colour that cannot be read, is reported as cannot prove, and each failure comes with a passing colour.
rules.values: at least 4.5:1; 3:1 at 24 px or 18.66 px bold; worst pixel over images and gradients

rules.statement: Content that moves on its own for more than 5 s, by animation, script or playing media, has a shown, focusable, labelled pause control that stops it from the keyboard, with and without script, and nothing moves on its own under reduced motion.
rules.values: over 5 s: a labelled pause control that stops it; still under reduced motion

rules.statement: A hero intro is skipped under reduced motion and when the page loads scrolled or at an anchor, and reaches its end state within 5 s when the film is blocked or play() is rejected.
rules.values: skipped under reduced motion or when loaded scrolled; end state within 5 s

rules.statement: Revealed content is revealed by the time the reader reaches the end of the page, runs its entrance once and is never hidden again when the reader scrolls back.
rules.values: run once; never hidden again

rules.statement: Headlines run 4-10 words and ledes 18-42 words; the bands were counted on a Vietnamese page and re-counted on English copy.
rules.values: headlines 4-10 words; ledes 18-42 words

rules.statement: A tile carries at most 2 calls to action.
rules.values: at most 2 calls to action per tile

rules.statement: Durations follow the motion classes: controls at most 300 ms, panels growing with distance within 240-480 ms, reveals 700-1100 ms; long reveals are never flagged against the control limit.
rules.values: controls at most 300 ms; panels 240-480 ms; reveals 700-1100 ms

rules.statement: A launch page holds at most 3 pinned set pieces (inferred).
rules.values: at most 3 pinned set pieces

rules.statement: Heavy set pieces (image sequences, several films, stacked blur) sit behind a low-memory gate that serves the static layout on low-memory devices and under Save-Data (inferred).
rules.values: device memory at most 2 GB or Save-Data: static layout

rules.statement: Every control shows a visible focus ring of at least 2 px.
rules.values: focus ring at least 2 px

rules.statement: Copy never invents awards, ratings, user counts or quotes; proof the user has not supplied appears as a marked placeholder.
rules.values: no invented proof; placeholders marked

rules.statement: Copy avoids hype words, and a headline that would still work with a competitor's name in it is rewritten around what only this product does (inferred).
rules.values: no hype words; headlines specific to the product

rules.statement: The hero headline stays legible at the narrowest slot width, 320 px, without overflowing its box or scrolling the page sideways (inferred).
rules.values: fits at 320 px

rules.statement: Every shell config, native-project copy and built bundle loads the origin the app is meant to load: the production origin for a remote shell, the bundled web build for a bundled one; a remote shell that would open its bundled build instead fails.
rules.values: loaded origin equals the expected origin; no server URL when the bundled build is expected

rules.statement: A shell config that ships, Tauri platform overrides included, never points at a loopback, unspecified, private-network, shared, link-local or local-network host, or at plain http; development URLs and options (server.cleartext, server.allowNavigation) stay in development-only settings such as devUrl or a live-reload config.
rules.values: a public https origin in every config that ships; no localhost, 127/8, 0/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, 100.64/10, ::1, ::, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, IPv4-mapped forms of these, .local, .lan, .internal or .home.arpa (a trailing dot included), or http

rules.statement: The native-project copy of the Capacitor config and the config inside the built app carry the same server URL as the project's config: after changing it, sync and rebuild before testing or shipping.
rules.values: server URL of the native copy and of the built bundle equals the project's

rules.statement: No page, frame or request of an app meant for a home-screen web app, an in-app browser, a WebView shell or an iframe answers with an HTTP Basic or Digest challenge; sign-in uses a login page and a session cookie.
rules.values: no 401 with a Basic or Digest challenge; a login page and a session cookie

rules.statement: After signing in, the session cookie (a host-only cookie from the app's own origin whose path covers the page, or the one named) comes back with the next request in WebKit; an app whose session cookie is Secure is served and tested over HTTPS, never plain http, localhost included.
rules.values: session cookie sent with the next request; HTTPS for Secure cookies, localhost included

rules.statement: An app signed in inside an iframe on another site gets no session cookie in WebKit, even one set SameSite=None; Secure: open it first-party, embed it from the same site, or ask for storage access from a tap.
rules.values: no session cookie in cross-site iframes, SameSite=None; Secure included

rules.statement: The origin a shipping shell loads carries no staging, dev, preview or test label in its host name, counting only whole labels left of the registrable domain.
rules.values: no staging, dev, preview or test host label in a shipping config

rules.statement: A remote shell carries only an offline page, not a full web build that it would open, frozen at build time, if its server URL were ever dropped.
rules.values: only an offline page beside a remote server URL

rules.statement: Web code that subscribes to Web Push inside a WKWebView shell needs a native remote-push plugin: WKWebView has no Web Push, and on iPhone and iPad Safari gives it only to web apps added to the Home Screen.
rules.values: a native remote-push plugin in a shell (local notifications do not count), or a home-screen web app for Web Push

rules.statement: A handler that observes effectiveAppearance (KVO, a Combine publisher or observeValue) marks a view for display or replaces its image or title only after comparing the light or dark match with the last one; an observer that redraws on every callback can feed itself through the menu bar snapshot and keep a core busy.
rules.values: redraw only when the light or dark match changes; the loop held one core at 90-97 % CPU

rules.statement: A widget that should offer options uses AppIntentConfiguration with a WidgetConfigurationIntent whose parameters use AppEntity types, keeping its kind string; StaticConfiguration offers nothing in Edit Widget, so it is wrong wherever the sources declare a configuration intent no AppIntentConfiguration uses, or the task asks for options.
rules.values: AppIntentConfiguration with a WidgetConfigurationIntent; kind string unchanged

rules.statement: After an install or self-update, no process of the app's extensions started before the bundle was installed or runs an executable outside it; the app stops stale extension processes, re-registers the extension with pluginkit -a and reloads all timelines at launch.
rules.values: extension processes start after the install and run the installed copy

rules.statement: Every widget snapshot entry fits its width and height inside its content margins and renders to a PNG of that size times the scale; content that needs more width or height than the widget has is capped or shortened before it ships, and every entry of a non-empty catalog writes its own PNG.
rules.values: needed width and height, margins included, at most the entry size; PNG of width and height times the scale; unique PNG names

rules.statement: Each widget snapshot PNG is byte-equal to the previous build's, or the difference is looked at and accepted by writing a new baseline.
rules.values: byte-equal to the baseline, or a reviewed --update

rules.statement: Write each widget kind once, as a shared constant that the widget and every reloadTimelines(ofKind:) call use, and never rename it after release: a new kind drops the widgets people placed.
rules.values: one kind constant per widget, unchanged after release

rules.statement: A WidgetConfigurationIntent used by AppIntentConfiguration declares at least one @Parameter; a list of choices is an AppEntity with an EntityQuery.
rules.values: at least one @Parameter; choices as an AppEntity with a query

rules.statement: A build made without Xcode runs the App Intents metadata extraction itself and lists the entity query, transient entity, intents package and dynamic options protocols, or the extracted metadata is incomplete and the options do not show.
rules.values: metadata extraction lists EntityQuery, TransientEntity, AppIntentsPackage and DynamicOptionsProvider

rules.statement: Render widget snapshots in several processes rather than one long run, since very many renders in one process can abort; the runner renders 40 entries per process by default and refuses more than 60.
rules.values: 40 entries per process by default; at most 60

rules.statement: Test a menu bar or widget app as a debug build with its own bundle identifier and data folder, never by replacing, stopping or re-registering the installed copy; capture its windows from inside the logged-in session.
rules.values: own bundle identifier and data folder; window capture from inside the session

rules.statement: A widget extension is sandboxed and signed with its own entitlements before the host app, whose signature must not replace them; it starts from its @main WidgetBundle, a notarized build carries a secure timestamp, and entitlements are probed from inside an app bundle.
rules.values: sandboxed extension with its own entitlements; WidgetBundle entry point; secure timestamp

rules.statement: A script never reads a .env file as shell code (source or a dot command of a .env file, export or eval of its text): a line with an unbalanced quote, a $( or an ampersand runs as a command and zsh prints the secret in its command not found message. Read one value with grep and cut and check only its length.
rules.values: no source, . , export $(...) or eval of a .env file; one value read with grep -E ^NAME= and cut -d= -f2-

rules.statement: With pipefail on, no pipeline ends in grep -q: grep exits at the first match, the command before it can be killed by SIGPIPE, and the pipeline then reports failure although it matched. Capture the output first, or let grep read everything with its output sent to /dev/null.
rules.values: no | grep -q, --quiet or --silent after set -o pipefail or setopt pipefail until it is turned off

rules.statement: An agent never handles an administrator password: no sudo -S or --stdin, no password in do shell script. A root command runs through do shell script with administrator privileges so macOS asks the person at the Mac, or the user runs the sudo command.
rules.values: no sudo -S, sudo --stdin or do shell script ... password; with administrator privileges and no password clause

rules.statement: AppleScript names its target application as a quoted literal, or inside a using terms from block: a tell application with a variable or an unquoted name does not load the dictionary when the script compiles, so the app's terms fail or mean something else.
rules.values: tell application "<name>" or tell application id "<bundle id>"; a variable only inside using terms from application "<name>"

rules.statement: Nothing that must persist lives under /tmp or /private/tmp: no git worktree or clone made there, and no launchd job whose program, arguments or working directory point there, because macOS deletes old files in that folder on its own schedule and at restart.
rules.values: no git worktree add or git clone into /tmp or /private/tmp; no Program, ProgramArguments or WorkingDirectory under them

rules.statement: A launchd property list passes plutil -lint and has a dictionary root, a Label, and Program or a non-empty ProgramArguments array of strings whose program is an absolute path; launchd looks a bare name up only in its short default PATH. The file is named <Label>.plist.
rules.values: plutil -lint OK; Label; Program or ProgramArguments[0] absolute; default launchd PATH /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin

rules.statement: A job is proven loaded before it is trusted: launchctl print finds its label in the domain named (system for a LaunchDaemon, gui/<uid> for a LaunchAgent), loaded from the property list on disk with the program and arguments that file holds now, and its last exit code is 0 or it never exited. An edited file applies only after launchctl bootout and bootstrap.
rules.values: found in the domain; loaded path equals the plist; loaded program and arguments equal the file; last exit code 0 or never exited; exit 113 means not found

rules.statement: Start a GUI app from an agent shell with env -i and only HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, TMPDIR and the system PATH, since open -a passes the calling environment, tokens included, to the app.
rules.values: env -i HOME USER LOGNAME SHELL TMPDIR PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin open -a <App>

rules.statement: In zsh, call the unified log as /usr/bin/log: log is a zsh builtin that lists logins.
rules.values: /usr/bin/log show or /usr/bin/log stream in zsh

rules.statement: Send a remote command over SSH in single quotes or as a here-document with a quoted delimiter, and run it in a login shell when it needs the user's PATH: in double quotes, $ and $( expand on the local machine first.
rules.values: ssh <host> 'zsh -lc ...' or ssh <host> 'zsh -ls' <<'EOF'

rules.statement: A launchd job that reaches a protected folder (an external volume, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, iCloud Drive) starts a dedicated binary rather than a shell or script interpreter, since macOS records privacy permission against the binary launchd starts; never grant Full Disk Access to a shell.
rules.values: a dedicated binary as the program of a job that reads protected folders; no Full Disk Access for /bin/sh, /bin/bash or /bin/zsh
